subtitle: Where are you going?
learning_focus: Ask where someone is going, invite them to do something together, and accept an invitation.
scene_summary: Continuation of the  first, polite introduction between Mali and Narin in an everyday setting.  Narin asks where she is going and invites her for coffee.
function_summary: Opening introductions and polite small talk.
speaker_a_role_summary: Adult woman with a polished, professional-adjacent presence; organized and polite.
speaker_b_role_summary: Central anchor character; calm, socially capable, dependable, connector between groups.
required_vocabulary_list:
- ที่ไหน (thîi-nǎi) = where
- ไป (bpai) = go
- ดื่ม (dʉ̀ʉm) = drink
- กาแฟ (gaa-faae) = coffee
- ยินดี (yin-dii) = pleased
- ด้วยกัน (dûai-gan) = together
allowed_vocabulary_list:
- คุณ (khun) = you
- ฉัน (chǎn) = I
- ชื่อ (chʉ̂ʉ) = name
- ผม (phǒm) = I
- สวัสดี (sà-wàt-dii) = hello
- อะไร (à-rai) = what
required_grammar_list: - Subject omission when clear: Leave out the subject when context already makes it obvious.
relationship_rules_list:
- lesson_1_can_start_here: This pair may begin the curriculum as a first meeting in greetings and introductions.
- keep_growth_gradual: Do not move this pair too quickly into intimacy; let familiarity develop over multiple lessons.
- no_fast_romance: Romantic potential must remain subtle and should not appear in early A1 lessons.
dialogue_constraints_list:
- short lines only
- one communicative move per line
- beginner-safe Thai only
- use polite particles consistently
- no flirting or intimacy
- no important new grammar outside lesson scope
- Mali uses ฉัน
- Narin uses ผม
must_avoid_rule: Only use vocabulary from Required vocabulary and Previously introduced vocabulary. Do not introduce additional vocabulary unless it is extremely basic and unavoidable for natural Thai.
